scenarios.context: Two friends talk after an argument.

speakerA.en: Hi, Reza. Can we talk? I think you're angry with me.
I know, and I'm really sorry. I didn't think it was a big deal.
You're right. It was my fault. I'll ask Sina not to tell anyone else.
I understand. Please give me another chance. I'll show you that you can trust me.

speakerB.en: Yes, I am. You told Sina my secret, and I trusted you.
It was a big deal for me. Now everyone in class knows.
Thanks. I'd like that, but I'm still disappointed.
Okay, I forgive you. Friends make mistakes sometimes, but don't do it again.

scenarios.context: Two friends make plans for the weekend.

speakerA.en: What are you doing this weekend, Mina? Do you have any plans?
How about going to the new park on Friday? We could have a picnic.
Then let's go on Saturday morning and watch a film on Friday evening instead.
Yes, the more the merrier. I'll bring the sandwiches if you bring the drinks.

speakerB.en: Nothing special yet. I'd like to do something fun. Do you have any ideas?
Good idea, but the forecast says it might rain on Friday.
Perfect. Should I invite Sara and Nina as well?
Deal. I'll send a message to the group now.

scenarios.scenario: Suggesting a solution to a teacher
scenarios.context: A class representative suggests an idea to the teacher.

speakerA.en: Mr. Karimi, we have a problem. Our classroom is very noisy at lunch break.
We could have a quiet corner for students who want to read or rest.
We can make the rules together, and a different student can look after it each week.
I think so. We can vote tomorrow and tell you the result.

speakerB.en: I've noticed that. Do you have any suggestions?
That's an interesting idea. How would we keep it quiet?
I like your suggestion. Would the class agree?
Good. Let's try it for a month and then decide if it works.

scenarios.context: A student feels stressed and asks a friend for advice.

speakerA.en: I'm so stressed. I have a test, a project and football practice this week.
No, I just try to do everything at the last minute.
But I'll have no time to relax.
Hmm, I don't want to miss football, but you may be right. I'll ask my coach.

speakerB.en: That's a lot. Have you made a timetable?
That's the problem. I suggest you list everything and do the hardest task first.
Plan short breaks, too. And maybe skip one practice before the test.
Good idea. If you want, I can help you make the timetable now.

scenarios.context: Two friends talk about how to save money for a bike.

speakerA.en: I really want a new bike, but it costs a hundred and fifty dollars.
Only forty dollars. I'm afraid it will take too long.
True. Maybe I could also earn money by washing our neighbours' cars.
I didn't think of that. I'll ask my parents tonight.

speakerB.en: That's a lot. How much have you saved so far?
Why don't you save a little every week? Even five dollars helps.
Great idea! You could also sell your old toys and books online with your parents' help.
In three months you could reach your goal. I'm sure you can achieve it.
